image_transform: Whole views; aspect-preserving fit into common tiles, padding and identical labels. No flip or content crop.
cadence: All recorded frames retained; 10 control frames per playback second; display only.

notes.text: Keep the grasp; cautiously reduce visible pitch offset and bring the plug toward the socket center while closing part of the vertical gap.
Plug is retained and nearly centered over the visible slot. Finish the small pitch correction and descend slowly, keeping clearance for final alignment.
The plug is almost vertically aligned with the slot. Lower by 2.5 mm with a very small lateral centering adjustment, retaining the current grasp and orientation.
The connector now reaches the mouth of the socket. Continue a short, straight downward insertion while preserving lateral alignment and grip.
Advance another 1.5 mm along the insertion direction. The socket remains fixed and the plug appears centered; monitor seating rather than interpreting tracking as success.
Continue a slow seating motion with only a 0.2 mm depth-axis centering correction; retain grip and check whether the visible body continues entering the slot.
Seating is visually uncertain: the plug body may have stopped moving with the fingers. Relieve contact by 1 mm and make a small pitch correction about the tip before another insertion attempt.
Apply a final small pitch adjustment while keeping the tip nearly stationary laterally, then cautiously re-advance 1.5 mm into the socket.
The plug appears flush with the slot. Use only a tiny final seating increment and hold the grasp to allow the contact to settle; completion is not yet confirmed.
Seating remains uncertain. Remove a small cross-axis tilt about the plug tip and slightly reduce commanded opening to limit visible slipping, with only 0.25 mm of descent.
Lift 2.5 mm to relieve the uncertain contact and verify that the plug follows the grasp before making a finer socket-depth alignment correction.
The plug did not visibly follow the small lift. Close the gripper further and retract only 3 mm to distinguish a slipping grasp from a connector caught at the socket mouth.
With the narrower grasp, retract 5 mm slowly to clear the socket lip and check whether the connector is retained before re-aligning.
The plug now visibly follows the lift and is centered above the opening. Re-approach the socket mouth with the established narrower grasp, preserving alignment.
The plug edge appears skewed relative to the slot. Back off 2 mm and make a modest yaw correction about the connector, checking the edge alignment before insertion.
Maintain clearance and continue the small yaw correction. Compare the exposed lower connector edge with the socket's long edge before re-approaching.
A residual slant remains on the exposed plug edge. Correct a small roll component about the tip while maintaining clearance and the closed grasp.
The lower plug edge now looks closer to parallel with the socket. Center it slightly left and descend 3 mm to approach the mouth, keeping orientation fixed.
The connector has reached the visible socket mouth. Attempt a slow 2 mm insertion with the corrected orientation and closed grasp, checking that the body moves rather than slips.
The exposed body appears slightly lower but seating remains uncertain. Continue only 1.5 mm straight down, retaining the current alignment and grip.
The fingers are approaching the block while the plug body stops descending. Leave the plug supported at the mouth, open slightly and raise the hand 6 mm to regrasp higher on the housing.
With the plug supported and clearly visible, level the open fingers and center them on its upper housing for a higher, unobstructed regrasp.
Close around the upper housing, then lift 2 mm to establish retention and clear the lip before correcting the plug's visible sideways lean.
Lift a further 4 mm with the closed regrasp. Check that the housing clears the socket lip before changing its alignment.
The lifted housing is visibly skewed. Correct part of its yaw and sideways lean while keeping the lower end near the socket center and maintaining clearance.
The correction improved the exposed edge. Reduce the remaining skew in smaller increments, keeping the tip above the slot and nearly stationary.
The exposed plug edge now looks nearly parallel to the slot. Approach by 3 mm with a small lateral centering correction, maintaining the higher grasp.
The plug has reached the socket mouth with clearance below the fingers. Attempt a slow 2 mm insertion without changing its corrected orientation.
The body may be catching at the lip. Make a small socket-depth alignment adjustment with slight initial relief, then probe downward gently; retain the centered lateral alignment.
Test the adjusted depth alignment with a short 1.75 mm straight insertion, watching for motion of the connector housing rather than finger motion alone.
The housing has stopped descending. Probe the poorly observed socket-depth direction by 3 mm with minimal downward travel, keeping the visible lateral alignment unchanged.
Depth translation alone did not visibly seat the housing. Relieve contact and test a small pitch correction about the lower end, preserving its approximate socket position.
Probe a few millimeters toward the camera while lowering slowly. The lower edge is visually parallel to the slot, but its depth alignment is still ambiguous.
Make a smaller reverse depth correction while lightly advancing downward. Keep the visible connector edge parallel and avoid a large seating push.
Refine the residual pitch and yaw with a tip-preserving motion, then gently re-enter. The lower edge is centered but full insertion is still not visible.
Shift the lower end slightly left to match the visible slot center and probe 1 mm toward the camera while gently lowering. Keep the corrected orientation fixed.
The housing is still stopped at the mouth. Lift 9 mm to remove contact and expose the lower connector for a fresh alignment check, keeping the grasp closed.
The newly exposed lower blade looks narrow/skewed. Raise it clear and test a small yaw change so its projected width and edge direction can be compared with the socket.
The exposed blade widened with the last yaw change. Continue that rotation above the socket while approximately holding its tip position; do not descend until the blade faces the opening.
Continue yaw alignment with the connector lifted. Its exposed broad face is becoming more visible; preserve clearance and check the lower edge against the slot.
The last yaw sweep obscured the blade and did not establish alignment. Return toward a broad face parallel to the slot while keeping the connector safely above it.
Complete the return toward the earlier parallel-edge orientation and descend only part of the visible gap. Keep the blade above the mouth for the next alignment check.
The exposed lower blade is narrower than the slot. Lift clear and rotate toward the direction that previously widened it, keeping its lower end approximately centered.
Continue the yaw search above the opening and recenter slightly left. Use the exposed lower blade, not the partly occluded upper housing, to judge alignment.
Correct the unintended pitch component from the preceding rotation while keeping the connector lifted; reassess the exposed blade before further alignment.
Keep the connector clear of the block and continue the yaw sweep to expose the full lower blade; compensate lateral motion approximately and reassess before descending.
The visible lower edge is broad and nearly parallel to the slot. Center it leftward and close only part of the vertical gap while holding this orientation.
The lower edge is centered with a small remaining gap. Approach the socket mouth by 3 mm, keeping the established yaw and closed grasp.
The connector has reached the socket mouth. Advance 2 mm slowly with fixed alignment; the housing is partly occluded, so seating remains uncertain.
Probe a further 1.5 mm downward without changing orientation. The fingers obscure the connector, so this is a limited seating attempt, not a completion claim.
Insertion is obscured and unconfirmed. Lift clear of the block and return toward a view that exposes the connector, keeping the grasp closed.
Keep the plug clear and undo the large yaw excursion to expose its face again. Re-establish visual alignment before any further insertion.
Keep clearance above the socket and turn the exposed connector closer to a face-on view, compensating approximately for tip motion. Recheck its lower edge before descending.
The lower blade is clearly too narrow in this view. Turn toward its broad face while maintaining clearance and approximately stabilizing the exposed tip over the socket.
The exposed blade widens with this yaw direction but is right of the socket. Continue the turn while recentering left and correcting the uncertain camera-depth offset, staying well above the opening.
The exposed lower edge is now broad and centered. Close most of the vertical gap while shifting slightly away from the camera, leaving a small clearance for the final approach.
Close the remaining small gap to the socket mouth without changing the broad-edge alignment. Check contact and finger clearance before attempting further insertion.
The connector is supported at the socket, but the fingers have little insertion clearance. Open and raise the hand 8 mm to regrasp higher on the housing.
With the connector supported, center the open hand over its upper housing and turn the fingers toward a face-on regrasp. Maintain the higher grasp height.
Finish leveling the open hand while the plug remains supported. The upper housing is now visible for a centered regrasp.
